PASS-WITH-NOTES — performance/294, F240, round one
Head: 7704c7ec932c514de975442ca1ae03d62abc6300
Base: 0587a416611096daa0712e96fe161f47b81e87d2
Answers: 01a1f98d-c8cb-73e3-a5f4-6bc08606f3a5
Worktree: /Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/review-294-7704c7e

No blocking performance finding against the requested ownership repair and configured fallback budget. P294-OBS1: the literal whole-exit 3-second wording is stronger than the evidence; the qualifications below are part of this verdict. Recommend a documentation qualification, not new bounded-log machinery without evidence of a normal-use hang. Reviewer integral-tiglon agrees with the nominal-wait qualification; prime/pm-001 owns any C34/F-item disposition, not assigned a number by this seat.

Ownership and allocation:
- control.rs330-357: the original 1-second caller reap still precedes handoff. A child reaped or no longer waitable there returns before the new shared slot or boxed closure. Normal teardown command, kill, leave-thread and successful deferred-reaper behavior remain.
- Only delayed handoff allocates one Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>> slot and one boxed FnOnce, plus one atomic Arc clone. There remains one named deferred-reaper thread attempt, not a retry loop. Slot/closure memory scales with outstanding delayed exits, not seats or steady fleet ticks; successful handoff retains it until the reaper runs. No global historical cap is introduced.
- A successful thread takes the Child exclusively; the temporary MutexGuard ends before child.wait(). Failed production Builder::spawn drops the unrun closure but leaves the caller's Arc/Child intact, so the caller can take and poll it. No ownership race found by source inspection.

Backpressure and shutdown composition:
- Existing REAP_WAIT=1s and REAP_POLL=5ms are reused once on failed deferred-thread admission: approximately200 additional nonblocking try_wait polls, roughly400 across both waits, with terminal checks and scheduling/syscall overhead. Polls launch no subprocess. Scaling is per exiting control client; E concurrent such waits gives roughly200E polls/s during that bounded failure path, not periodic per-seat work.
- The refactored loop checks status before its deadline guard, so a terminal try_wait may occur at/after the deadline where the old loop first checked time. Treat1s as configured wait, not an exact syscall-count or hard real-time ceiling.
- Caller timeout sums are1+1s normally and1+1+1s only on deferred-thread admission Err. This does not independently deadline synchronous thread creation/kill, inherited outer state-lock admission, or scheduling overhead.
- NEW Left diagnostic at control.rs298-303 is synchronous eprintln after both reap waits. daemon_log.rs23-36 and60-67 redirect stderr to a blocking UnixStream pair; its reader95-120 writes/flushes the original sink under a mutex. [INFERENCE] backpressured stderr/logger/sink can therefore hold that diagnostic outside the timeout sum. No private or live logging stall was observed by this seat; the Err tests invoke reap_with, not the logging wrapper. Do not read the docs'3s whole-exit wording as a proven end-to-end deadline. It is the configured wait budget under timely non-wait operations/logging.
- Existing F242 release is concurrent with HTTP/workers. Its5s is HTTP listener-drain time, not a deadline around release_control or the whole daemon. The3s configured client wait fits numerically below5s, but does not prove a5s stop. Later admitted-write/store cleanup has another deadline; inherited join/state-lock ceilings remain.
- If the child outlives both waits and no reaper can start, Left explicitly returns it and logs only its PID; it can still be left unreaped. F240 repairs silent loss on admission error, not unconditional zombie elimination.

Steady state:
No new production recurring loop, timer, per-request/per-seat task or daemon process launch site. Same existing leave/reaper threads; the new fallback uses the existing bounded reap loop, once more on Err only. Existing pathological helpers may persist; no new claim of a fleet-wide helper cap. No CPU/RSS/spawn savings are claimed.

Verification:
Read exact-head clean-tree/diff receipt artifact://344 (3 files,133 insertions/15 deletions), relevant unchanged caller/constants and logger source. Reviewer integral-tiglon independently ran one nice19, locked, four-job shared-build batch at this head: fmt --all -- --check; clippy -p pij-tmux --all-targets -- -D warnings; test -p pij-tmux, exit0. Direct retained raw excerpt: /Users/jordanknight/.copilot/session-state/a14ff8eb-a4ad-4780-a956-5a72a5065fbf/files/pr294-rust-validation.log. 110 passes:40lib/2.05s,41adapter/58.46s,23control_mode/6.46s,6control_teardown/0.29s. Includes both injected admission-Err cases, real thread handoff and real tmux teardown cases. Injected Err is not an observed kernel thread-exhaustion event. Author MA/MB/MC claims were not rerun or independently attested by performance. Full harness receipt is pending, not a pass.

Read-only performance seat: no product edits, builds, tests, mutations, reload, bounce or extra live collection. The two separately requested delayed F242 single-ps RSS jobs remain scheduled; no new window or sampler for294. Static cost receipt: /tmp/performance-294-static-cost.json.

Harness feedback:
magicWand: distinguish configured timeout sums from whole-operation deadlines in teardown review packets, explicitly including diagnostics after the timer.
difficulties: stdio logging has its own blocking boundary; source-level wait sums and tests below the diagnostic cannot establish a whole-exit maximum. Captured here under the read-only review contract; no product-tree ledger/retro edits.

Retain performance/294 until merge. This clears performance for this exact head only; independent role and ship gates remain separate.
